subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — session topology intake and decision log
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@luminexa.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Luminexa Procurement <procure@luminexa.ai>
Date: 2029-03-12 09:12 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake — request for session topology and decision log

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday. Luminexa is moving quickly on our recommender + search feature and procurement has asked for more detail to size a dedicated Redwood fleet for a pilot (and to include in our internal SOW). Specifically, they want:

- a completed sizing questionnaire capturing peak concurrency, steady-state qps, typical prompt & response lengths, and retry behavior;
- a simple "decision log" showing recommended GPU SKUs, quantization options you'd propose for a pilot, and fallback model variants; and
- an estimate of pilot duration and burst allowances we should request in the contract.

I've attached a short prompt-mix sample and a CSV with a few representative session traces. Can you send the questionnaire back with your recommendations, or let us know if you need more telemetry? Procurement would prefer a completed intake by EOD Monday so they can move to legal.

Best,
Samira
CTO, Luminexa

Attachments: luminexa-prompt-mix-sample.json (text), sample-session-traces.csv (csv)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@luminexa.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-12 11:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — request for session topology and decision log

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the traces.

Attached is our sizing matrix (luminexa-sizing-matrix.xlsx) and a decision-log template (redwood-decision-log-template.docx) pre-filled with a pilot recommendation. High-level notes in the spreadsheet:

- Peak concurrency for pilot: we need your confirmation, but based on traces we see short bursts to ~650 concurrent sessions for 90s windows. We estimated a pilot target of 200 peak concurrent sessions sustained for 2 weeks to validate mixed-read/write workload.
- Prompt/response mix: sample shows median prompt 80 tokens, median response 220 tokens. We modeled both transactional (single-turn) and multi-turn sessions with KV cache reuse — see sheet "PromptMixModel".
- GPU SKU recommendation: 2x A800-80GB per shard for the pilot (quantized INT4 where acceptable). Fallback model: a smaller 7B variant on 1x A10G for low-cost durability during off-peak.
- Batching & latency: continuous batching with 30–50ms added scheduling latency gives 15–20% token-cost savings while holding p95 generation latency within your 300ms SLO for single-turn requests.
- Retry/timeout behavior: treat client retries at >500ms as duplicates — configure idempotency token tracking and a short 3s server-side request timeout to avoid queue build-up.

Quick ask: can Marissa get a short sample of your peak-hour traffic (UTC timestamps + request sizes) so we can run a one-off queueing/occupancy sim? If procurement needs the questionnaire in a different format, we can convert it.

I'll leave Marissa to the details on telemetry and Ben to coordinate the contractual pilot parameters.

Thanks —
Irene
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: luminexa-sizing-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-decision-log-template.docx (docx)

From: Samira Khan <samira@luminexa.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Luminexa Procurement <procure@luminexa.ai>
Date: 2029-03-13 08:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — request for session topology and decision log

Thanks Irene — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from procurement & infra:

> On Mar 12, 2029, Irene Choi wrote:
> > we see short bursts to ~650 concurrent sessions for 90s windows. We estimated a pilot target of 200 peak concurrent sessions sustained for 2 weeks

We can commit to the 200-peak pilot. The traces we provided earlier were from an internal stress run; production should be ~220 peak with a 5% daily growth assumption. We attached a short CSV of peak-hour traces for your sim.

Questions:
- Can you confirm whether the INT4 recommendation will affect semantic quality on our re-ranker model? We care about NDCG and will need a short A/B plan if quantization causes regressions.
- For the fallback 7B model, do you recommend pinning it behind the same routing policy or using a regionally separate pool? Our compliance team prefers regional isolation for EU customers (we'll flag that in the SOW).

Also, procurement wanted the decision log to include an explicit pilot end-state acceptance criteria. We propose:
- p95 latency <= 350ms for single-turn;
- production NDCG delta vs. baseline <= 0.015;
- no more than 2 unplanned failovers in the pilot window.

I'll upload the peak-hour sample now.

—Samira
CTO, Luminexa

Attachments: luminexa-peak-hour-sample.csv (csv), luminexa-prompt-mix-sample.json (json)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@luminexa.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-15 16:28 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — request for session topology and decision log

Hi Samira — glad we landed on pilot targets. Next steps I propose: 

1) Pilot mutual action plan: 
   - Week 0: finalize SOW and pilot resource commit (2x A800-80GB per shard, reserve burst pool up to 3x for first 48 hours) — DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/LX-045-pilot
   - Week 1–2: pilot validation window (200–220 peak as agreed); collection of evals / NDCG tests; Marissa to run occupancy sim and tune batching thresholds.
   - Week 3: review meeting to decide go/no-go for expansion.

2) Technical owners: Marissa will run the sim and give a short report by 2029-03-19. Irene will provide the finalized decision-log with explicit quantization tradeoffs by 2029-03-18.

3) Acceptance criteria: we'll align on yours (p95 <= 350ms, NDCG delta <= 0.015, <=2 unplanned failovers). If those pass, we'll propose a phased committed capacity plan and pricing.

Can procurement confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) and preferred region for the pilot? I'll wait for their reply and will start the DocuSign process once we have the SOW sign-off.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
